waters.working: Up from 106 a day ago - a modest push of fresh water through the pocket water, so trade the long-leader game for weighted caddis and stonefly nymphs on the seams, and let the extra color cover your approach to the undercut banks.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 24.9 ft and falling - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Half a foot off the midweek bump and settling - shad are the forage, so a white swimbait across the wing-dam seams at first light stays the play.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.9 ft - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Steady at normal pool and clearing - a crawfish-pattern crankbait ticked along the riprap and the lock wall, with a jig for the barge cuts once the sun gets up.

waters.reading: Sound highs 8:57 AM at 3.5 ft and 9:20 PM at 4.0 ft at Hampstead; lows 3:11 AM and 3:22 PM, both 0.6 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 8:57 AM and 9:20 PM in the sound.
waters.working: One night past full at 100% - spring tides still, so the long ebb off the 8:57 high will pull hard toward the 3:22 PM low; that fall is the red drum window on the oyster bars and grass edges, finger mullet or shrimp on the bottom. Water 83.1F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast. The Fisherman's Post monthly, published Aug. 2 and 26 days old, has the surf giving up whiting and black drum on shrimp - and flounder season opens in the sound Tuesday.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No watches, warnings or advisories posted for coastal North Carolina this morning per the National Weather Service.
